nt(n, str(v)[:1600])\nPY\"", "aggregated_output": "Click **New case** in the suite header (or in the empty-state screen when no ca
ses exist yet) to open the case workspace. The case is a draft until you press **Save**: backing out without saving leaves your su

ite unchanged.

### Case workspace

The case editor is a two-pane workspace. The left column is where you write the case; the
right column shows the selected trial: a live run in progress, a persisted iteration from history, or a spec preview.\n\n**Left co
lumn: the case spine**\n\nEvery case opens in the spine, however it was authored: in the app, through the CLI, or from an SDK suit
e file. The spine is a flat, ordered list of steps. Each step is one of:\n\n* **Prompt**: a user turn the model receives. The firs
t prompt is always present; use **Add assertion or action** to add a second prompt for multi-turn cases.\n* **Interact**: a widget

interaction (click, typing) run against a live widget.
* **Assert**: an assertion that grades the case.

Below the step list,

an **Expected outcome** field holds the goal sentence the judge grades against.

**Assertions**

Use **Add assertion or action
** to add an assertion, a second prompt, or an interact step. Each assertion row says what it checks, who wrote it, and what a mis
s does:\n\n* **Route**: answers \"which tool should handle it?\" and carries that answer's strictness: *Reach the tool* allows ext
ra calls, *Exact route* requires the exact order with no extras. The route is always Required.\n* **Step N**: an assertion written
as a step (what the CLI and the SDK produce). It is graded in place, at its position in the run, and is labelled by that position
: a step-level \"no tool errors\" reads **No tool errors so far**, because it only sees the transcript up to that point. Editing o
ne rewrites that step; it never becomes a case-level assertion.\n* **This case**: an assertion you added here. It is graded once,
over the finished transcript.\n* **Suite**: a default the suite applies to every case. Read-only here, with a link to the suite's
**Checks by stage** settings.\n\nThe list reads as a checklist with progressive disclosure. An off row shows only its short name.
Once on, clicking the name opens an inline editor showing the full criterion, the **Required / Advisory** role control, and any ed
itable fields (thresholds, match criteria). Multiple editors can stay open at once. An assertion that carries a number (such as a
latency budget) shows it under the name at rest.\n\nA row's **role** says what a miss does: **Required** fails the trial, **Adviso
ry** shows the miss without failing it. The control appears when your deployment supports assertion policy; otherwise the role chi
p shows read-only with a tooltip explaining why it cannot be changed, for example, when the assertion is inherited from the suite,
or when the backend does not yet support assertion policy.\n\nBecause a failing required assertion halts the run, an assertion wr

itten as a step can leave later assertions unrun. The trial column marks those **Skipped**.

**The route question**

The answe

r here is what marks a case negative: never an inference from its steps:

* **A named tool**: the case must take that route.
*
**No tool should be called**: a negative case. It passes only if the model called nothing. An assertion that requires a tool call
contradicts this, and the spine says so.\n* **Any route**: the case names no route and is graded by its assertions. This is a norm
al positive case, and it is what most CLI- and SDK-authored cases are.\n\nA brand-new case that asserts nothing at all must answer
this question before it can be saved or run: without an assertion, a goal sentence, or a named tool, it would pass vacuously.\n\n
**Expected outcome**\n\nThe **Expected outcome** field below the step list holds the goal sentence the judge grades against. The h
int under it says what the judge will actually grade against:\n\n* A **goal sentence**: the judge grades against it, and the suite
's criteria still apply.\n* **No sentence, but a route**: the judge grades against the expected route.\n* **Neither, but suite cri
teria**: the judge grades against those.\n* **None of the above**: the judge grades against the request itself, with its score cap

ped at 0.85.

**Skip the judge for this case** turns the judge off for this case only. It applies to the next saved run.

**Sa
ving and running**\n\nSave and Run are disabled while any JSON field in the case (such as tool arguments) holds invalid JSON. The
field is highlighted and a tooltip explains what to fix. Correct the field to re-enable both buttons.\n\n**Right column: the selec
ted trial**\n\nThe trial opens on its **Scorecard**: the same scorers the left column lists, in the same order, each with what hap
pened to it on this trial. The scorecard is one column of stage sections, in user-value chain order. Each section is headed by the
stage name and a state chip (passed, failed, or a neutral label); under the heading sits at most one sentence about the stage as
a whole: the AI note when one exists, else the recorded floor, else the chain's own reason for a failure no row explains. Then eve
ry evaluator that grades that stage appears as an **Expected / Actual** pair separated by hairlines. **Expected** is the configure
d criterion; **Actual** is the AI-generated narrative when one is current, else the recorded reason and evidence, else the formatt
ed value, else \"No observation recorded.\"\n\nConnection, Discovery, Tool call, and Response each lead with a **Built-in** runner
check row: a locked row that reports what the stage analysis decided, in the same Expected / Actual form as your evaluators. It n
ever gates a trial and is not counted in the summary line. Tool call and Response runner checks appear only when the case gives th
e runner a call or response to measure.\n\nThe summary line counts **required rows only**: \"2 of 2 required passed · 1 advisory\"
. An advisory miss is shown on its row and never counted as a failure, because it did not fail the trial. A scorer with no result
reads **Not measured** rather than passing by default. The verdict word itself stays in the header above.\n\nThe judge's row hosts
the judge panel, so labelling a trial works where the judge sits. Under the rows, **Score rows** expands the raw score contract,
including any row the backend could not join.\n\n**Chat**, **Tool Calls** and **Trace** show the transcript, and **Steps** shows e
xecution order, with the same assertion names the rest of the page uses and the reason under a failed step.\n\nThe right column re

solves to one of these views, in precedence order:

1. **Explicit history pick**: a trial you selected from History.
2. **Live
run**: a quick run is in progress.\n3. **Latest**: the most recent persisted iteration with a trace.\n4. **Spec preview**: the aut

hored steps rendered as a conversation preview.
5. **Empty**: no trial yet; start typing a prompt.

> [!NOTE]
>
> A **negativ
e case** is one you marked **No tool should be called**. Meta questions (\"what params does `search` take?\"), conversational drif
t, and ambiguous prompts are the usual shape. A case that simply names no tool is *not* negative. It is graded by its assertions.\

n
### History inspect

Click **History** in the trial header to open a list of past iterations. Selecting one freezes the left
form on that trial's snapshot (the exact steps, assertions, and settings that were in effect when it ran) so you can compare what
you see in the trace against what was authored at the time.\n\nWhile a trial is frozen, an **Inspecting** banner appears at the to
p of the left column. If the current draft differs from the frozen snapshot, a **Changed** indicator appears. Click **Edit case**

to return to the live draft; the selected trial stays visible on the right.

### Next run sheet
